details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> CUDA: fuse FFN gate/up matmuls and GLU in MMQ with interleaved gate/up rows (#29948) * cuda: fuse FFN gate/up and GLU in MMQ with interleaved gate/up rows For prompt processing, run the gate and up matmuls of a dense FFN as one mul_mat_q launch and apply the GLU in the write-back. - The loaders take the gate weights as a second pointer and fill the weight tile with up and gate rows interleaved in chunks of 8, so each thread holds an up value and the matching gate value (rows r and r + 8 of an MMA tile). - The MMA loop is unchanged: same tile, warp layout, vec_dot and one sum[] per thread. The fused write-back computes the GLU from registers and writes half the rows. - The fused path uses the regular tiling (no stream-k) with the column tiles innermost so that neighbouring blocks share weight tiles. - Enabled for Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0 and IQ4_XS on NVIDIA Turing and newer. * cuda: assert the fused MMQ gate argument and trim redundant comments * cuda: move the fused MMQ h

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> llama-quant : fix 4D tensor quantization using ggml_nrows() and name-based expert detection (#30820) * llama-quant : fix quantizing 4D tensors nrows_total was ne[1]*ne[2], so for a 4D tensor only the first ne[2] slices were quantized and the rest of the rows were dropped. Use ggml_nrows(tensor) to count all rows, including ne[3]. Fixes #29916 * llama-quant : detect expert tensors by name and fix imatrix size for 4D tensors The MXFP4_MOE path used ne[2] > 1 to detect MoE expert tensors. This is wrong for non-expert tensors with 3 or more dims, e.g. MLA projections (BailingMoE3) and 4D conv kernels. Use the tensor name instead: all tensors used by GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID are named *_exps or *_chexps. This also removes the BailingMoE3 special case. The imatrix holds one vector of ne[0] values per 2D slice, so the expected size is ne[0]*ne[2]*ne[3], not ne[0]*ne[2]. This matches how the imatrix is indexed per row for 4D tensors in llama_tensor_quantize_impl. Assisted-by: Claude O

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> common, grammar: add recursive depth limit, make it a requirement (#31153) * common, grammar: add recursive depth limit, make it a requirement * catch more recursive functions * common : tidy up peg parser changes * grammar : reject candidates in a loop, without a depth limit The depth limit in llama_grammar_reject_candidates_for_stack counted the code points of a vocab token, so any token of 256 chars or more was always rejected under a grammar, such as the 512-space token of GLM-4.7-Flash or the long space tokens of Laguna-S-2.1. The rejection now walks the code points with its own stack of levels instead of recursing: there is no limit and no stack risk, whatever the length of a token from the GGUF, and the masks match master. * grammar : track rejected candidates as indices into the input At a given code point a candidate only differs from its input by the position of its code point pointer, so the levels now carry indices into the input candidates instead of copies.
